title: Food Fortification and Eat Right Challenges in India
shortDescription: Why fortification works, how FSSAI regulates it, and the double burden Eat Right India is trying to solve.
genZNote: India's got hidden hunger AND rising obesity at the same time — fortification and Eat Right are the plot-twist fix.

sections.heading: Fortification Vocabulary
sections.body: Mass fortification suits widely eaten, centrally processed staples (salt, wheat flour, rice, edible oil, milk). The FSS (Fortification of Foods) Regulations, 2018 specify levels; products carry the "+F" logo. Salt iodisation began in the 1960s–70s for goitre control; Universal Salt Iodisation is the long-running programme. Fortified rice has been integrated into government schemes (ICDS, PM POSHAN, PDS) with a national rollout by 2024.

sections.heading: Eat Right India — Aspects and Challenges
bullets: Launched in 2018: three pillars — Eat Safe, Eat Healthy, Eat Sustainably.

Challenge 1 — double burden: undernutrition (stunting, wasting, anaemia) coexists with overweight, diabetes and hypertension; NFHS-5 (2019–21) reported stunting ~35.5% and anaemia ~57% among women 15–49 (check for newer NFHS rounds).
Challenge 2 — ultra-processed/HFSS foods, sugar-sweetened beverages, high salt; "Eat Right" encourages reduction of fat, sugar and salt.
Challenge 3 — industrial trans fat: FSSAI limited trans fat to 2% of oils/fats; WHO called for global elimination.
Challenge 4 — adulteration and unsafe street food: Clean Street Food Hubs, hygiene ratings, FoSTaC.
Challenge 5 — food waste and sustainability: Save Food, Share Food; RUCO for used cooking oil.
Tools: Eat Right Campus, Station, School, Workplace; Eat Right Mela; Hygiene Rating; school safe-food regulations restricting HFSS foods near schools.

sections.heading: Limits of Fortification
sections.body: Fortification supplements — it does not replace dietary diversity; excess intake (e.g. preformed vitamin A, iron in thalassaemia/sickle cell conditions) needs caution, and levels must be monitored through market surveillance.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Fortification adds micronutrients to staple foods to prevent deficiency, while Eat Right India promotes safe, healthy and sustainable diets amid a double burden of malnutrition.
keyFacts: Eat Right India: 2018; pillars Eat Safe, Healthy, Sustainably.
Iodised salt, fortified rice/wheat/oil/milk are key vehicles.
Industrial trans fat limit: 2% in oils/fats.

highYieldFacts: Enrichment restores lost nutrients; fortification adds new ones.
Fortified rice via PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN.
commonTraps: Do not call high-iron bajra "fortified" — it is biofortified.
